- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior period.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33), model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to reflect risk aversion bias.
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior period), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; apply a 1–3% downward correction.
- If model forecast is significantly below recent 5-day average (e.g., < 95% of 5-day MA), consider mean reversion bias — increase forecast toward historical mean.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture sentiment-driven momentum; if sentiment is trending upward, add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for next 5–7 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag by 1–3 days; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead if sentiment is trending.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67), model often overfits short-term noise; use 3–5 day moving average to smooth forecast.
